moon.name: The Moon
moon.composition: Rocky, with a small iron-rich core
moon.surface: Heavily cratered, with dark volcanic maria and bright highlands
moon.description: Earth's only natural satellite and the fifth largest moon in the Solar System, tidally locked so the same face always points toward Earth.
notable_features: Tidal locking keeps one face permanently toward Earth
Maria (dark plains) formed from ancient volcanic activity
Highlands are older, heavily cratered terrain
Drives Earth's ocean tides
Site of the Apollo crewed landings

phobos.name: Phobos
phobos.composition: Carbon-rich rock, possibly a captured asteroid
phobos.surface: Heavily cratered, dominated by the large Stickney crater
phobos.description: The larger and closer of Mars's two small moons, orbiting so fast it rises and sets twice each Martian day.
notable_features: Orbits Mars faster than Mars rotates
Slowly spiraling inward, likely to break apart in tens of millions of years
Dominated by the giant Stickney impact crater

deimos.name: Deimos
deimos.composition: Carbon-rich rock, possibly a captured asteroid
deimos.surface: Smoother than Phobos, with a regolith-covered surface
deimos.description: The smaller, outer moon of Mars, with a smoother appearance than its companion Phobos.
notable_features: Smallest of the two Martian moons
Smoother surface, partly covered in loose regolith
Likely a captured asteroid, like Phobos

io.name: Io
io.surface: The most volcanically active body known in the Solar System
io.description: A moon wracked by intense tidal heating from Jupiter's gravity, making it the most volcanically active body known.
notable_features: Hundreds of active volcanoes
Tidal heating from Jupiter and neighboring moons drives its activity
Surface colored by sulfur compounds

europa.name: Europa
europa.composition: Ice shell over a probable liquid water ocean, rocky interior
europa.surface: Smooth ice crust crossed by long fractures
europa.description: An ice-covered moon thought to hide a deep, salty subsurface ocean beneath its cracked icy crust — a major target in the search for habitability.
notable_features: Smooth icy surface with few craters
Strong evidence of a subsurface liquid water ocean
Long linear fractures crisscross the surface

ganymede.name: Ganymede
ganymede.composition: Rock and ice, with a metallic core
ganymede.surface: Mix of old, dark cratered terrain and younger grooved terrain
ganymede.description: The largest moon in the Solar System, larger than the planet Mercury, and the only moon known to generate its own magnetic field.
notable_features: Largest moon in the Solar System — bigger than Mercury
Only known moon with its own internally generated magnetic field
Likely harbors a subsurface ocean

callisto.name: Callisto
callisto.composition: Roughly equal parts rock and ice
callisto.surface: One of the most heavily cratered surfaces in the Solar System
callisto.description: An ancient, heavily cratered moon that has changed little since the early Solar System.
notable_features: Among the most heavily cratered bodies known
Geologically quiet compared to its neighbors
Possible subsurface ocean beneath the ice crust

titan.name: Titan
titan.atmosphere: Thick, nitrogen-methane atmosphere denser than Earth's
titan.composition: Rock and ice core beneath a thick icy shell
titan.surface: Lakes and seas of liquid methane and ethane, dune fields
titan.description: Saturn's largest moon and the only moon in the Solar System with a substantial, thick atmosphere and stable liquid on its surface.
notable_features: Thick, hazy nitrogen-rich atmosphere
Lakes and seas of liquid methane and ethane
Complex weather cycle similar in principle to Earth's water cycle, but with methane

enceladus.name: Enceladus
enceladus.atmosphere: Very thin, water vapor near the south pole
enceladus.composition: Ice shell over a subsurface liquid water ocean
enceladus.surface: Bright, icy, with active geysers at the south pole
enceladus.description: A small, brilliantly reflective moon whose south-polar geysers spray water-ice particles from a subsurface ocean into space.
notable_features: Active geysers erupt from 'tiger stripe' fractures at the south pole
Feeds material into Saturn's E ring
Subsurface ocean makes it a key astrobiology target

rhea.name: Rhea
rhea.atmosphere: Extremely thin, oxygen and carbon dioxide
rhea.composition: Mostly water ice with some rock
rhea.description: Saturn's second-largest moon, an icy, heavily cratered world.
notable_features: Second largest moon of Saturn
Icy composition with a heavily cratered surface
May have a very tenuous ring of its own

iapetus.name: Iapetus
iapetus.surface: Strikingly two-toned, one hemisphere dark and one bright
iapetus.description: Known for its dramatic two-tone coloring, with one hemisphere dark as coal and the other bright as snow.
notable_features: Extreme brightness contrast between leading and trailing hemispheres
A prominent equatorial ridge gives it a walnut-like shape
Orbits far from Saturn on an inclined path

dione.name: Dione
dione.surface: Cratered with bright, wispy fracture patterns
dione.description: An icy moon with bright, wispy streaks that are actually ice cliffs revealed by later imaging.
notable_features: Bright wispy terrain later revealed to be ice cliffs
Shares its orbit with two smaller trojan moons
Moderately cratered icy surface

titania.name: Titania
titania.composition: Roughly equal parts ice and rock
titania.surface: Canyons and fault systems cutting across cratered terrain
titania.description: The largest moon of Uranus, marked by huge canyons that suggest past geological activity.
notable_features: Largest moon of Uranus
Massive canyon systems, some deeper than Earth's Grand Canyon
Evidence of past internal geologic activity

oberon.name: Oberon
oberon.composition: Roughly equal parts ice and rock
oberon.surface: Old, heavily cratered surface with some canyons
oberon.description: The outermost of Uranus's major moons, an ancient, heavily cratered world.
notable_features: Second largest moon of Uranus
Dark reddish material coats parts of the surface
One of the most heavily cratered Uranian moons

miranda.name: Miranda
miranda.surface: Extreme, jumbled terrain including giant canyons and terraced ridges
miranda.description: A small moon with a bizarre, patchwork surface featuring some of the tallest cliffs known in the Solar System.
notable_features: Verona Rupes may be among the tallest cliffs in the Solar System
Chaotic, jumbled terrain suggests a violent geological history
Smallest of Uranus's five major moons

ariel.name: Ariel
ariel.surface: Bright, relatively young surface with canyons and fault valleys
ariel.description: The brightest moon of Uranus, with a relatively young surface shaped by past geologic activity.
notable_features: Brightest of Uranus's major moons
Networks of valleys and fault scarps
Relatively few large craters suggest a younger surface

umbriel.name: Umbriel
umbriel.surface: Dark, heavily cratered, among the least reflective moons in the Solar System
umbriel.description: The darkest of Uranus's major moons, an ancient and heavily cratered world.
notable_features: One of the darkest moons in the Solar System
Old, heavily cratered surface with little sign of resurfacing
Featureless bright ring on its surface remains unexplained

triton.name: Triton
triton.composition: Rock and ice, likely a captured Kuiper Belt object
triton.description: Neptune's largest moon, unusual for orbiting backward (retrograde) — strong evidence it is a captured dwarf planet from the Kuiper Belt.
notable_features: Orbits Neptune in retrograde, unlike most large moons
Active nitrogen-gas geysers have been observed
Likely a captured Kuiper Belt object similar to Pluto
